column1: 佛在舍衛國祇樹給孤獨園。
column2: The Blessed One was living in the town of Srāvastī at Jetavana in the pleasure-garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.

column1: 時有一梵志。 祇樹間有大稻田，
column2: At that time there was a Brahman who had in Jeta-vana a large rice-field, that was already ripe.
At any moment (lit.
morning and evening), it was ready to be reaped.

column1: 梵志晨起， 往到田上， 遙見禾穟，
column2: The Brahman got up one morning, went up to the field and had a look far away at the ears of the paddy.
He was delighted at heart.
He said to himself that he had his wish fulfilled.
He looked at the corn, was much enamoured of it and would not leave [the sight of] it.

column1: 佛是時從諸比丘， 入城求食，
column2: The Buddha, at that time, followed by the mendicants, entered the town and begged alms.
He saw from a distance that the Brahman was thus happy.

column1: 便謂諸比丘： 「汝曹見是梵志不？
column2: Then he said to the mendicants "Do you see this Brahman?"
All of them said in reply "Yes."
The Buddha silently entered the town.
After eating food, everyone returned to the pleasure-garden.
The same night it rained heavily and there was a great [shower of] hail.
All the crop in the field was destroyed.

column1: 梵志有一女， 亦以夜死。
column2: The Brahman had a daughter, who also died that night.

column1: 梵志以是故， 愁憒憂煩，
column2: Because of this, the Brahman was sad, perturbed, annoy- ed and grieved.
He began to cry and nobody could stop him.

column1: 明日， 眾比丘持應器入城求食，
column2: Next day the Assembly of the mendicants took their begging bowls, entered the city and begged alms.

column1: 便聞梵志有是災害， 啼哭甚悲，
column2: They then heard that such and such a calamity had fallen upon the Brahman, who cried and was very sad.

column1: 非沙門、梵志、及國人所能解其憂者。
column2: No śramaṇa or Brahman could deliver him from sorrow.

column1: 比丘食竟， 還到佛所，
column2: The mendicants finished the eating of food and came back to the place where the Buddha stayed.
They paid their homage to the Buddha, and explained to Him the mental condition [as explained above] of the Brahman.

column1: 」言適竟， 梵志啼哭， 來到佛所，
column2: Immediately after their speech, the Brahman came crying to the place where the Buddha was.
He inquired of the health of the Buddha and sat by his side.

column1: 佛知其本憂所念， 即謂梵志言： 「世有五事， 不可得避，
column2: The Buddha knew his sorrowful thoughts and then said to him: "There are five things in this world, which cannot be avoided and from which there is no escape."

column1: 亦無脫者。 何等為五？
column2: Which are those five things?

(i) There are things which must wane or diminish.
欲使不耗減， 是不可得；	Even if one wishes that they may not diminish, it is impossible.
當亡棄法，	(ii) There are things which must come to ruin.
欲使不亡棄， 是不可得；	Even if one wishes that they may not be ruined, it is impossible.
當病瘦法，	(iii) There are things which must be diseased.
欲使不病瘦， 是不可得；	Even if one wishes that they may not be diseased, it is impossible.
當老朽法，	(iv) There are things which must grow old.
欲使不老朽， 是不可得；	Even if one wishes that they may not grow old, it is impossible.
當死去法，	(v) There are things which must perish.
欲使不死去， 是不可得。	Even if one wishes that they may not perish, it is impossible.
「凡人無道、無慧計， 見耗減、亡棄、老、病、死法來，	An ordinary man who knows no Path and has no wisdom sees things waning, coming to ruin, getting diseased, growing old, and perishing.
即生憂憒悲哀， 拍髀熱自， 耗身無益。	Then follows suffering, tribulation, grief, lamentation, beating of the chest with hot breath, and tormentation, with no avail.
何以故？	Why should it be so?
坐不聞知諦，	Because, he sits without hearing and knowing the Truth.
當如是。 梵志！ 我聞有抱諦者， 見耗減法、亡棄、老、病、死法來， 不以為憂。	Thus, O Brahman, I hear that he who has grasped the Truth does not become sorrowful, even when he sees things waning, coming to ruin, getting diseased, growing old and perishing.
何以故？	Why should it be so?
已聞知諦， 當如是。 不是獨我家耗， 世悉亦爾。	Because, he has already heard and known the truth that [such bewailing] is harmful not only to his family, but to the whole world.
世與耗俱生，	The world is born along with this waning of things.
我何從獨得離？	How can I alone be free from it?
慧意諦計， 我今已耗， 至使憂之，	The wise man thinks over the truth thus: 'I am already suffering, causing grief to myself.
坐羸不食，	I am feeble. I do not eat anything.
面目委色，	My face and eyes have lost their lustrous appearance.
與我怨者快喜、與我厚者代憂， 慘慼家事不修計耗，	Over me the enemy is delighted. Kind people share my sorrow, share the grief and misfortune of my family, and wish that such a calamity may not occur again.'
不可復得。 已諦如是， 見耗減、亡棄、老、病、死法來， 終不復憂也。	Thus when he has seen the truth, that things must wane, must come to ruin, must get diseased, must grow old and must perish, he would never be grieved.
」佛以是因緣， 為梵志說偈： 「不以憂愁悲聲， 多少得前所亡？	On this account the Buddha said to the Brahman the following stanzas (gāthā): (1) Because of sorrow and grief, there should be no piteous lament Over things, small or great, that have been [already] lost.
痛憂亦無所益， 怨家意快生喜。	Of no avail are the sorrow and grief, that merely gladden The enemy's heart, and do make him rejoice.
至誠有慧諦者， 不憂老病死亡，	(2) The man of faith, who has wisdom and Truths [realised], Has no sorrow, old age, disease, nor death or dissolution.
欲快者反生惱， 見其華色悅好。	Happiness doth one crave, but tribulations doth one create; A flower doth one see, and its colour doth he admire.
飛響不及無常， 珍寶求解不死，	(3) The colour is so momentary, that even a stroke or a bird's flight cannot compete; The precious things should one seek, knowing that they will not die.
知去不復憂追， 念行致勝世寶。 諦知是不可追，	Knowing the passing away [of things], the sorrowful things he doth not pursue, But mindfulness doth he practise, and the transcendent Treasure doth he gain.
世人我卿亦然， 遠憂愁念正行， 是世憂當何益？	(4) Truly doth he know that they do not deserve to be pursued----- These men of the world who, like you and me, are all alike; From sorrow and grief, he studiously doth keep himself off, [For], of what avail can all this, of the world, be?
」 佛復為梵志極說經法， 次說布施、持戒， 現天徑欲善，	Further the Buddha spoke to the Brahman on several sūtra-dharmas, such as talk on charities, good conduct,heavens, advantages and disadvantages and lack of solidity of worldly pleasures.
其惡無堅固。 佛知梵志意軟向正， 便見四諦。	When the Buddha came to know that his mind had become soft and inclined [towards Him], He made him see the Four Truths.
梵志意解，	The Brahman's mind understood them.
便得第一溝港道， 如染淨繒， 受色即好。	Then he attained the First Path—Srotāpatti-mārga; just as a clean piece of silk cloth well receives the dye at once.
